summary: Ron Garry works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and teacher Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer (1932–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under teacher Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz works in Tibetology and sociology. His appointments include Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser (b. 1956) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Koshin Ogui in 1985 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1989–1995) and San Francisco State University (~1995).

Ronald Egan (b. 1948) is a Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held posts at Harvard (~1978–1987), Wellesley College, UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2012; emeritus ~2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick (1937–2001) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and Tibetan studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oxford (~1961–1964) under Harold Walter Bailey and served as Professor at the University of Hamburg (1971–2001).

Ronald Inden (b. 1940) is an Indologist and historian. He served at the University of Chicago (attested 2007), where he is attested in 2026 as Professor Emeritus of History and South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist, Tibetan, and Indic studies. He earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley in 1985, studied under numerous academic and traditional teachers, and held a post at Fairfield University (attested 2002–2005).

Ronald Neufeldt (b. 1941) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Calgary, beginning as Associate Professor around 1977, attested in 2001, and attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Ronald Y. Nakasone (b. 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1980. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1991) and the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng (1894–1983) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and held a post at Yenching University (~1926–1941).

Rongdao Lai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her Ph.D. at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and held posts at the Center for Chinese Studies and McGill University.

Rory Lindsay works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and Harvard University, completing his Ph.D. at Harvard under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp in 2011 alongside numerous other teachers.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under Peter Harvey and served as a teacher at International Christian College.

Rosalind O'Hanlon earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London in Indology and history. She served as Professor in Indian History and Culture at the University of Oxford (~2006–2020) and is an Emeritus Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge.

Rosan Ikeda (b. 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1960–1969). He held successive academic ranks at Komazawa (1969–2012; Professor 1983–2012) and headed the Sōtō Zen Center for Advanced Studies in 2009.

Rosane Rocher (b. 1937) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles under Ludo Rocher. She was a Research Fellow at the FNRS (1961–1970) and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1970.

Rosemarie Fuchs (b. 1950) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr (b. 1946) is a linguist and Indologist. After earning her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg and habilitating at Regensburg, she held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and served as Indogermanische Gesellschaft president (2004–2016).
Rosemary Radford Ruether (1936–2022) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).
